items.description:
What's this LoRA

This is a LoRA trained on a particular style. It creates images with a bright color palette and shading. The training dataset contained some images underwater or with fishes, so you'll need to add those to the negative prompt if you don't want them.

The images in the examples are created using only this LoRA and different models (mainly my custom: https://civitai.com/models/24149)

You don't need to specify a word to trigger this LoRA.

The LoRA works very well also on NSFW (check last examples).

items.name: Underwater photo LoRA - tropical edition
items.description:
This model was finetuned on top of Realistic Vision 2.0 to depict underwater photography. Rather than capturing photos from all types of ocean environments (e.g. deep waters with odd looking fish), wanted to focus only on well-lit photos from shallow waters. 

Training images were selected for high resolution, good lighting, and colorful subjects (like fish and coral). Was particularly interested in photos that showed A) light reflecting on the surface of the water, B) light rays coming into the water or C) light reflecting on the ocean floor. 

For training - used a relatively higher learning rate (3e-4), a larger LoRA (128 rank / 64 alpha) and most importantly, high noise offset (0.3) for high contrast and vivid colors. 

Join our Discord for any questions or feedback!

Prompting

Use “underwater photo” to trigger the style of the trained LoRA. Append the recommended positive prompt terms from Realistic Vision, but skip the recommended negative prompts unless you are depicting human subjects underwater (which I have not tried).

Recommend using LoRA at around 0.8. 

Example prompts

  • Underwater photo of colorful fish and coral <lora-underwater-000390-0.8>, 8k uhd, dslr, soft lighting, high quality, film grain, Fujifilm XT3 2

  • Underwater photo of fish <lora-underwater-000390-0.8>, 8k uhd, dslr, soft lighting, high quality, film grain, Fujifilm XT3

Coral can kind of float sometimes, as the LoRA hasn’t fully learned that coral is supposed to be attached to rocks and stuff. This LoRA also oddly struggles with dolphins. 

Settings

Resolution must be 768 x 768 for best results.

Sampler = DPM++ SDE Karras

Sample images were using CFG = 7 and 25 inference steps.

items.name: Underwater specialization|coral and stone (actually more than that)
items.description:
I found a new AI tool Shakker, a best image to image tool. You can try it via https://www.shakker.ai

The production of this Lora actually originated from helping a friend to take pictures of seawater corals, but the available models found were not particularly suitable.

The training source uses some real pictures and some midj5.2 images, 768*768 is the original training size

The main trigger word is "underwater" and "close up" can be used to increase the close-up draw rate. The weight is recommended to be 0.6-0.9

There will be some nice light and shadow, and then there is a high probability of coral (possibly strange succulents) and stones

It can have a good performance in 2D-real style (it can cooperate with my other Lora to produce a real sea view chassis)

items.name: FLUX Underwater Photography - The Aesthetic World of the Deep Sea
items.description:
Flux's Lora model for underwater photography, named Lora Underwater, aims to capture the mystery and beauty of the underwater world, providing you with boundless inspiration for your creations.

It can authentically recreate the lighting effects of the underwater environment, including the refraction on the water surface, the scattering underwater, and the color variations at different depths. This allows you to create realistic underwater photography works without actually diving into the water.

items.name: Underwater style mix
items.description:
Attempting to teach AI underwater stuff. Combines images from multiple sources including Amanchu!, Rou (rou22) and saver (artbysaver).

It is better at doing underwater stuff in general. This model can do underwater content in various styles and is not limited to the styles in the training data.

I recommend prompting for an artist style. Any style. The default style of the lora is a bit odd.

In negative prompt you can use "sepia" quite often. "Amanchu!", "monochrome", "greyscale", and "artist name" can help if they try to push through.

It can still do all the trained styles too. Saver, Amanchu! styles and Rou are better than the older individual loras.

V2:

Trained on Illustrious v1.0. Trained on 3207 images for 13400 steps. After repeats and batches this is 24 epochs of the primary trainig dataset. Images from other anime were added to stop model from learning "Amanchu!" style so strongly.

It is now better at generalizing style. Amanchu still often pushes through but not as badly as before.

Various things like diving masks, scuba gear, and diving poses are better.

Rou style is not broken anymore.

It is now a LoCon.

V1:

Training details: 942 images from Amanchu!, 634 images from Rou, 771 images from Saver.

Trained on Illustrious v0.1 for 5 epochs (5868 steps).
